title: How Russians See the War in Ukraine

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: As Russia steps up its bombing campaign against Ukrainian cities, it's also waging another battle over the truth about the war.
sentences.zh: 随着俄罗斯加紧对乌克兰城市的轰炸，它也在关于战争真相的问题上发动了另一场战争。

sentences.en: My colleague, Valerie Hopkins, on why so many people in Russia are in denial about what is happening, even as it wrecks the lives of their own family members in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我的同事瓦莱丽·霍普金斯将讲述为什么这么多俄罗斯人对正在发生的事情视而不见，尽管这正在摧毁他们在乌克兰家人的生活。

sentences.en: It's Monday, March 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月14日，星期一。

sentences.en: Valerie, you've been reporting on the war in Ukraine since the beginning.
sentences.zh: 瓦莱丽，你从战争一开始就在报道乌克兰局势。

sentences.en: And you've been hearing stories again and again of this pretty shocking misinformation campaign coming from Russia.
sentences.zh: 你不断听到关于俄罗斯发起的这场相当令人震惊的虚假信息运动的故事。

sentences.en: Can you describe what you've been hearing and seeing?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下你所听到的和看到的吗？

sentences.en: You know, I've been talking to a lot of people here in Ukraine, first when I was in Kiev and then on the road,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在这里和很多乌克兰人交谈过，起初是在基辅，后来是在路上，

sentences.en: and a lot of them have pretty shocking stories about their relatives in Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们中很多人都有关于在俄亲属的令人震惊的故事。

sentences.en: You know, Ukraine and Russia are really well-connected.
sentences.zh: 你知道，乌克兰和俄罗斯的联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: Millions of Ukrainians have relatives in Russia.
sentences.zh: 数百万乌克兰人在俄罗斯有亲戚。

sentences.en: Some of them used to live there.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人曾经住在那里。

sentences.en: But now, as some of Ukraine's cities are being bombed, as millions of people are being forced to flee, people are trying to tell their relatives in Russia what's going on.
sentences.zh: 但现在，随着乌克兰的一些城市遭到轰炸，数百万民众被迫逃离，人们试图告诉他们在俄罗斯的亲戚正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And they're being met with denial, resistance, and kind of a refusal to believe what their family members, their blood relatives, are telling them.
sentences.zh: 但他们得到的却是否认、抵触，以及一种拒绝相信他们的家人、血亲所说的话的态度。

sentences.en: And one person whose story really stuck out to me was this guy, Misha Katsurin.
sentences.zh: 有一个人的故事让我印象特别深刻，他叫米沙·卡苏林。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Oh, hi.
sentences.zh: 哦，嗨。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Do you hear me?
sentences.zh: 你能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Misha is 33 years old.
sentences.zh: 米沙今年33岁。

sentences.en: He lives with his wife and kids in Kiev and actually owns a really trendy chain of Asian restaurants.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子孩子住在基辅，经营着一家非常时髦的亚洲连锁餐厅。

sentences.en: Right now, of course, all my restaurants closed.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在我所有的餐厅都关门了。

sentences.en: And he said the fourth morning of the war.
sentences.zh: 他说在战争的第四天早上，

sentences.en: I realized that the father still didn't call me, like, any time.
sentences.zh: 我意识到父亲还是没有给我打过任何电话。

sentences.en: He woke up and realized that he hadn't heard from his dad at all since the war started.
sentences.zh: 他醒来后意识到，自战争开始以来，他根本没有收到父亲的任何消息。

sentences.en: And I thought maybe he doesn't know what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 我心想，也许他不知道这里发生了什么。

sentences.en: His father lives in Russia in a city called Nizhny Novgorod.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲住在俄罗斯一个叫下诺夫哥罗德的城市。

sentences.en: So I called him because that was strange.
sentences.zh: 所以我给他打了电话，因为这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: There is a war.
sentences.zh: 现在是战争时期。

sentences.en: I'm his son and he doesn't call me.
sentences.zh: 我是他儿子，他却不给我打电话。

sentences.en: So he gave his dad a call and told him what was going on.
sentences.zh: 于是他给父亲打了电话，告诉了他正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: I tried to tell him, how is it going here in Kiev with my family that Russia started bombing us,
sentences.zh: 我试着告诉他，我在基辅和家人现在的处境，俄罗斯开始轰炸我们，

sentences.en: that Russia started the invasion, and that I'm trying to evacuate my children, my wife, my family.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯发动了入侵，我正在努力疏散我的孩子、妻子和家人。

sentences.en: Everything is extremely scared.
sentences.zh: 一切都非常可怕。

sentences.en: And, like, that's real war.
sentences.zh: 而且，那是真正的战争。

sentences.en: But he said his father had a really different version of events and didn't really believe him.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，他父亲对事件的看法完全不同，而且并不相信他。

sentences.en: And he started to interrupt me.
sentences.zh: 他开始打断我。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, stop.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，停下。

sentences.en: Everything is like this.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: And he started to tell me how the things in my country are going on.
sentences.zh: 他开始告诉我我的国家正在发生什么。

sentences.en: He said his father basically said, no, no, no, and that he denied what Misha was telling him that he sees with his own eyes.
sentences.zh: 他说他父亲基本上就是说“不，不，不”，否认米沙亲眼所见并告诉他的事实。

sentences.en: So he told me that, look, everything is going like this.
sentences.zh: 所以他告诉我，看，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: So the Nazis, they took the government, the Nazis, the Ukrainian Nazis, and they are now control.
sentences.zh: 纳粹夺取了政权，纳粹，乌克兰纳粹，他们现在掌权了。

sentences.en: And anyways, he said, the government there, they're all Nazis.
sentences.zh: 总之，他说那里的政府全是纳粹。

sentences.en: So, Valerie, I'm going to stop for a second on this Nazi reference because it keeps coming up.
sentences.zh: 瓦莱丽，我先打断一下关于“纳粹”的说法，因为这个词反复出现。

sentences.en: This is an idea that Russian President Vladimir Putin has often repeated, right?
sentences.zh: 这是俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京经常重复的观点，对吧？

sentences.en: But why is he doing that?
sentences.zh: 但他为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't really make sense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: But for Putin, it's this weird multilayered argument.
sentences.zh: 但对普京来说，这是一个奇怪的多层论点。

sentences.en: He is trying to piggyback on the proud legacy of the Soviet defeat of the Nazis in World War II.
sentences.zh: 他试图利用苏联在二战中战胜纳粹的光荣遗产。

sentences.en: And he also cannot really deal with the fact that Ukraine wants to have a separate country and a separate identity from Russia 30 years after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 而且他也无法接受乌克兰在苏联解体30年后，想要拥有一个独立国家和独立身份的事实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Putin sort of sees this Ukrainian rejection of Russia, which has only gotten stronger since Russia invaded Crimea and now gotten even stronger.
sentences.zh: 普京把这种乌克兰对俄罗斯的排斥视为民族主义，这种排斥在俄罗斯入侵克里米亚后变得更强，现在更是如此。

sentences.en: He sees all of this as nationalism and that nationalism he kind of immediately starts to equate with Nazism in order to get support for this invasion.
sentences.zh: 他把这一切都视为民族主义，并为了获得入侵支持，将其与纳粹主义等同起来。

sentences.en: So essentially when he says this, he's trying to paint Ukrainians as crazy nationalists.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，当他这么说时，他是在试图把乌克兰人描绘成疯狂的民族主义者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I mean, he's actually used those words to refer to President Volodymyr Zelensky, who's actually Jewish and also a native Russian speaker.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他甚至用这些词来指代弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基总统，而泽连斯基实际上是犹太人，也是以俄语为母语的人。

sentences.en: President Putin has referred to him and the people around him as, quote, drug-addled Nazis on Russian TV, even though this is just a completely outlandish,
sentences.zh: 普京总统在俄罗斯电视台上称他和周围的人为“吸毒成瘾的纳粹”，尽管这完全是荒谬的、

sentences.en: intentional distortion of the truth.
sentences.zh: 蓄意的真相扭曲。

sentences.en: So Misha's dad is getting this idea from Putin's messaging, which is carried by Russian television.
sentences.zh: 所以米沙的父亲是从普京的宣传中得到这个想法的，而这些宣传是通过俄罗斯电视台传播的。

sentences.en: What else did Misha's dad say that he believes about the war in Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 米沙的父亲还说了什么他所相信的关于乌克兰战争的事情？

sentences.en: Well, he certainly doesn't think a full-scale war is actually happening.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他当然不认为一场全面战争正在发生。

sentences.en: Misha's dad thinks it's essentially a rescue operation conducted by the Russian military.
sentences.zh: 米沙的父亲认为这本质上是俄罗斯军队进行的一次救援行动。

sentences.en: And not only that, he believes that Russian soldiers are liberating Ukrainians from this repressive Nazi government and that the majority of the people want them there.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他还相信俄罗斯士兵正在从这个压迫性的纳粹政府手中解放乌克兰人，而且大多数民众希望他们在那里。

sentences.en: I told him, look, father, look, I'm here right now and I see it with my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，看，父亲，看，我现在就在这里，我亲眼所见。

sentences.en: So look how it's going on in reality.
sentences.zh: 看看现实中正在发生什么。

sentences.en: So it's pretty unbelievable that a father is denying his own son's reality.
sentences.zh: 一个父亲否认自己儿子的现实，这真是令人难以置信。

sentences.en: But how pervasive is this?
sentences.zh: 但这有多普遍呢？

sentences.en: Is this most Russians' view of the war right now?
sentences.zh: 这是目前大多数俄罗斯人对战争的看法吗？

sentences.en: So we actually have seen some pretty significant street protests in Russia, mostly in large cities since the invasion started, actually more than in Russia's recent history.
sentences.zh: 自入侵开始以来，我们确实在俄罗斯看到了一些相当大规模的街头抗议，主要是在大城市，实际上比俄罗斯近年来的历史都要多。

sentences.en: These people are out in the streets chanting no to war, even though they know that they'll likely be taken away by the police and detained.
sentences.zh: 这些人走上街头高喊“反对战争”，尽管他们知道自己很可能会被警察带走并拘留。

sentences.en: But we've also seen reports from Russian cities, including one done by this independent media outlet, Nastoyashyevdeme, or Current Time,
sentences.zh: 但我们也看到了来自俄罗斯城市的报道，包括独立媒体机构“现时”所做的一项调查，

sentences.en: which went out and spoke to Russian citizens and showed them pictures of the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他们走上街头采访俄罗斯公民，并向他们展示乌克兰战争的照片。

sentences.en: And their responses were, no, that's not happening.
sentences.zh: 他们的反应是：不，那不是真的。

sentences.en: These photos are fake.
sentences.zh: 这些照片是伪造的。

sentences.en: Ukraine was preparing for an attack on Russia.
sentences.zh: 是乌克兰准备攻击俄罗斯。

sentences.en: I'm absolutely convinced of that.
sentences.zh: 我对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: And I'm for Putin.
sentences.zh: 我支持普京。

sentences.en: They're essentially repeating what they've been hearing from Putin and from talk show hosts on state TV.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上是在重复他们从普京和国家电视台脱口秀主持人那里听到的话。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's really hard to get an accurate picture of public sentiment in Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，要准确了解俄罗斯的公众情绪真的很难。

sentences.en: For a pollster now, just asking that question could land them in jail or shut their organization down.
sentences.zh: 对于民调人员来说，现在问这个问题可能会让他们入狱或导致机构被关闭。

sentences.en: But what this video and what my reporting suggests is that this essential, complete denial of what's happening in Ukraine is actually pretty common in Russia.
sentences.zh: 但这段视频和我的报道表明，这种对乌克兰正在发生的事情的彻底否认，在俄罗斯其实相当普遍。

sentences.en: Valerie, what did you think as you were watching these man-on-the-street interviews?
sentences.zh: 瓦莱丽，你在观看这些街头采访时是怎么想的？

sentences.en: What was going through your mind?
sentences.zh: 你当时在想什么？

sentences.en: I was really sad, but I guess I wasn't so surprised.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常难过，但我想我并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a product of years and years of clamping down on free press and increasingly escalating rhetoric in media,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是多年来压制新闻自由和媒体言论日益升级的产物，

sentences.en: demonizing the other and slowly building the case for something exactly like this.
sentences.zh: 妖魔化对方，并慢慢为像现在这样的事情制造借口。

sentences.en: I think I was most shocked, actually, when there was a guy who literally looked into the camera, looked at the photos and said, Russia's not bombing Kyiv.
sentences.zh: 我最震惊的其实是一个人直视镜头，看着照片说：俄罗斯没有轰炸基辅。

sentences.en: It's like this alternate reality for so many people.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，这就像是一个平行现实。

sentences.en: And it's fascinating for me to try and understand why and how that can be.
sentences.zh: 试图理解为什么以及如何会变成这样，对我来说非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《交易手册》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的“交易手册峰会”上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过NYTimes.com免费直播部分采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费新闻访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So, Valerie, we're talking about Russians who don't believe what's happening to their own relatives,
sentences.zh: 所以，瓦莱丽，我们谈到了那些不相信自己亲人遭遇的俄罗斯人，

sentences.en: who don't believe and don't want to look at these photographs of bombings in Ukrainian cities.
sentences.zh: 那些不相信也不愿看乌克兰城市被轰炸照片的人。

sentences.en: And I think that this leads us to the question of why.
sentences.zh: 我认为这引出了一个问题：为什么？

sentences.en: What do you think it has to do with?
sentences.zh: 你认为这与什么有关？

sentences.en: Well, I think it has a lot to do with Vladimir Putin and Russia's relationship to him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这与弗拉基米尔·普京以及俄罗斯与他的关系有很大关系。

sentences.en: Putin came to power at this really critical time for Russia in 2000, a decade after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 普京在2000年这个对俄罗斯至关重要的时刻上台，那是苏联解体十年后。

sentences.en: And in the intervening period, there was just this total economic upheaval.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，经历了彻底的经济动荡。

sentences.en: You know, people knew what to expect in the Soviet period, even if they didn't love it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们在苏联时期知道会发生什么，即使他们并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: And now there was just this period of total uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 而现在，却是一个充满彻底不确定性的时期。

sentences.en: Anger is building in Russia among people with nothing else to lose.
sentences.zh: 在俄罗斯，那些一无所有的人心中积聚着愤怒。

sentences.en: They face a winter of empty bellies, infrequent heating and nothing to hope for but spring.
sentences.zh: 他们面临着一个饥肠辘辘、供暖不足的冬天，除了春天，别无希望。

sentences.en: Prices skyrocketed and people just couldn't afford basic necessities.
sentences.zh: 物价飞涨，人们根本负担不起基本生活必需品。

sentences.en: For the fifth day in a row, panicky Russians tried to withdraw their savings from banks, while the country's financial system appeared to teeter on the brink of collapse.
sentences.zh: 连续五天，恐慌的俄罗斯人试图从银行提取存款，而国家的金融体系似乎摇摇欲坠，濒临崩溃。

sentences.en: Half of the economy disappeared.
sentences.zh: 一半的经济消失了。

sentences.en: These Arctic coal miners took the mine director hostage after enduring more than six months without pay.
sentences.zh: 这些北极煤矿工人在忍受了六个多月没有工资后，扣押了矿长。

sentences.en: People were living in lawlessness.
sentences.zh: 人们生活在无法无天的状态中。

sentences.en: One local leader accusing Moscow politicians of behaving in a way that humiliates the Russian people.
sentences.zh: 一位地方领导人指责莫斯科政客的行为羞辱了俄罗斯人民。

sentences.en: There was a lack of trust in the government.
sentences.zh: 政府缺乏信任。

sentences.en: And many people, they don't believe in the ideals which existed in the former Soviet Union, and the new ideals hadn't been invented for them.
sentences.zh: 许多人不再相信前苏联存在的理想，而新的理想又没有为他们建立起来。

sentences.en: And there was also this really major loss of national pride that I think a lot of people discount.
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为很多人低估了那种严重的民族自豪感丧失。

sentences.en: They don't believe in their future.
sentences.zh: 他们不相信自己的未来。

sentences.en: So, I think that many people, especially in the West, saw this moment as Russia's chance to create democratic institutions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为许多人，特别是在西方，曾将这一时刻视为俄罗斯建立民主制度的机会。

sentences.en: To live in Moscow today is to watch the soul of a city die.
sentences.zh: 今天生活在莫斯科，就像看着一座城市的灵魂死去。

sentences.en: But many Russians associated this period in the 90s with instability, economic fear, and this rampant capitalism that didn't really help them.
sentences.zh: 但许多俄罗斯人将90年代的这段时期与不稳定、经济恐惧和猖獗的资本主义联系在一起，这些并没有真正帮助他们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember that time because I was there then.
sentences.zh: 我记得那个时代，因为我当时就在那里。

sentences.en: I started in 1994 in Russia.
sentences.zh: 我1994年开始在俄罗斯工作。

sentences.en: And I remember we saw the collapse of the Soviet Union as, you know, a chance to be free, a wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们当时把苏联解体看作是一个获得自由的机会，是一件美妙的事情。

sentences.en: And I think that by the end of the 1990s, many Russians had experienced it as a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 但我认为到90年代末，许多俄罗斯人已经将其视为一场悲剧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we have to recognize that that wasn't people's priority back then.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为我们必须承认，那不是当时人们的首要任务。

sentences.en: It was putting food on the table and not getting mugged by hooligans in the street and being able to trust the police and the law enforcement and the institutions again.
sentences.zh: 当时的首要任务是填饱肚子，不在街上被流氓抢劫，能够再次信任警察、执法部门和机构。

sentences.en: And through all of this, the personal and national shame and difficulty...
sentences.zh: 经历了这一切，个人的和国家的耻辱与苦难……

sentences.en: In Russia today, the clear winner of the Russian presidential election, Vladimir Putin, began to establish the Putin era.
sentences.zh: 在今天的俄罗斯，俄罗斯总统选举的明确获胜者弗拉基米尔·普京开始建立“普京时代”。

sentences.en: Into that situation walks Vladimir V.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，弗拉基米尔·V·

sentences.en: Putin.
sentences.zh: 普京登场了。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin, the career spy, talks about establishing what he calls a dictatorship of the law.
sentences.zh: 职业间谍出身的弗拉基米尔·普京谈论建立他所谓的“法律专政”。

sentences.en: Fight corrupt bureaucrats and strengthen the central government.
sentences.zh: 打击腐败官僚，加强中央政府。

sentences.en: Promising to take control and just promising stability, which is what people craved the moSt.
sentences.zh: 承诺掌控局面并带来稳定，这正是人们最渴望的。

sentences.en: Fifteen years after the fall of the Soviet Union, Moscow is now a 24-hour town.
sentences.zh: 苏联解体十五年后，莫斯科现在成了一座24小时不夜城。

sentences.en: The economy started to stabilize and a middle class actually emerged that was substantially better off in the years after Putin came to power.
sentences.zh: 经济开始稳定，中产阶级确实出现了，他们在普京上台后的几年里生活状况大大改善。

sentences.en: The streets pulse with the kind of big money that was once considered a capitalist abomination.
sentences.zh: 街道上涌动着曾经被视为资本主义罪恶的大量资金。

sentences.en: It's largely opportunistic wealth that Russia has enjoyed since the country's oil started selling on global markets for $45 a barrel.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是俄罗斯自石油开始以每桶45美元的价格在全球市场销售以来所享有的投机性财富。

sentences.en: He got massively lucky with oil prices and, you know, that sort of allowed the standard of living to rise
sentences.zh: 他在油价上运气极好，你知道，这在某种程度上让生活水平得以提高。

sentences.en: and cemented the trust that, you know, many ordinary Russians were living better under Putin than they ever had before.
sentences.zh: 并巩固了这样一种信任，即你知道，许多普通俄罗斯人在普京治下的生活比以往任何时候都要好。

sentences.en: President Putin today criticized the way many private businessmen, known as oligarchs, had bought state properties at bargain prices after the breakup of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 普京总统今天批评了许多被称为寡头的私人商人，在苏联解体后以低廉的价格收购国有资产的方式。

sentences.en: They appreciated him as a strong guy who was promising to clamp down on oligarchs.
sentences.zh: 他们视他为一位强人，并赞赏他承诺打击寡头。

sentences.en: You know very well what privatization was like in the early 1990s.
sentences.zh: 你很清楚20世纪90年代初的私有化是什么样子。

sentences.en: At that time, some market participants got multi-billion dollar state assets using different tricks.
sentences.zh: 当时，一些市场参与者利用各种手段获得了数十亿美元的国有资产。

sentences.en: And Putin continues to exert ever more control over Russian society.
sentences.zh: 而普京继续对俄罗斯社会施加越来越大的控制。

sentences.en: The Kremlin controls the most powerful news broadcasts on the three main television networks.
sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫控制着三大电视网中最有影响力的电视新闻节目。

sentences.en: He starts to bring the national media to heel to make sure that things that he doesn't like or criticism of him don't appear in the media.
sentences.zh: 他开始让国家媒体服从，以确保他不喜欢的事情或对他的批评不会出现在媒体上。

sentences.en: Russia's only independent media owner was formally charged today with embezzling state funds.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯唯一的独立媒体所有者今天被正式指控挪用国家资金。

sentences.en: His media outlets are known for criticizing the government.
sentences.zh: 他的媒体机构以批评政府而闻名。

sentences.en: And while some people were concerned more or less from the beginning of his rise, the majority of the people really accepted it.
sentences.zh: 虽然有些人从他崛起之初就开始感到担忧，但大多数人确实接受了这一点。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin is popular at home because of the economy based on energy.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京在国内受欢迎，是因为其基于能源的经济。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin remains easily the most popular politician across this vast country.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京依然是这个广袤国家中最受欢迎的政治家，这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the social contract that Putin made.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是普京达成的社会契约。

sentences.en: He said to the Russian people, I'm going to bring you order.
sentences.zh: 他告诉俄罗斯人民，我会给你们带来秩序。

sentences.en: I'm going to crack down on the oligarchs.
sentences.zh: 我会打击寡头。

sentences.en: I'm going to make it so that your life is stable.
sentences.zh: 我会让你们的生活变得稳定。

sentences.en: Your salary is reliable.
sentences.zh: 你们的工资是有保障的。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you're not going to mess with politics.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你们不能干涉政治。

sentences.en: And you're going to be OK with a media that is not free.
sentences.zh: 而且你们要接受一个不自由的媒体环境。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And while Putin largely consolidated his power over the last two decades, he did leave some pockets, you know,
sentences.zh: 虽然普京在过去二十年里很大程度上巩固了他的权力，但他确实留下了一些空间，你知道，

sentences.en: mostly online media, some radio spaces where people who didn't support the government,
sentences.zh: 主要是网络媒体，还有一些广播空间，在那里，那些不支持政府的人，

sentences.en: who were free in thinking and independent minded could air their views and hear people who mostly thought like them.
sentences.zh: 那些思想自由、独立思考的人，可以表达他们的观点，并听到那些与他们想法基本一致的人的声音。

sentences.en: You know, it wasn't mainstream national news on the airwaves, but you could find it if you looked for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这虽然不是广播中主流的国家新闻，但如果你去寻找，还是能找到的。

sentences.en: So bring us up to the war, Valerie.
sentences.zh: 那么，瓦莱丽，带我们了解一下战争的情况吧。

sentences.en: I mean, if Putin has been doing this for years, chipping away at independent media, what's different now?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果普京多年来一直这样做，一点点蚕食独立媒体，现在有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Well, now it's not chipping anymore.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在已经不是蚕食了。

sentences.en: It's a sledgehammer.
sentences.zh: 而是重锤出击。

sentences.en: He's been trying very hard to control the narrative around the war.
sentences.zh: 他一直在非常努力地控制围绕这场战争的叙事。

sentences.en: Which he refers to only as a, quote, special military operation.
sentences.zh: 他只将其称为“特别军事行动”。

sentences.en: That's why most Russians don't know what's really happening in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大多数俄罗斯人不知道乌克兰到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: The Kremlin today...
sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫今天……

sentences.en: And most of the official communications about it don't even mention the Russian military.
sentences.zh: 而且关于此的大多数官方通讯甚至都没有提到俄罗斯军队。

sentences.en: The state censorship office has now blocked the BBC Russian language service.
sentences.zh: 国家审查机构现已封锁了英国广播公司（BBC）的俄语服务。

sentences.en: That is a huge source of independent news here.
sentences.zh: 那是这里一个巨大的独立新闻来源。

sentences.en: The state orders some of the few remaining independent media in Russia to stop broadcasting, including the BBC's Russian service and the German broadcaster Deutsche Welle.
sentences.zh: 国家下令俄罗斯仅存的几家独立媒体停止广播，包括BBC俄语服务和德国广播公司德国之声。

sentences.en: And then it bans Facebook.
sentences.zh: 然后它封禁了Facebook。

sentences.en: And on the same day, the lower house of parliament, the state Duma, approves a law forbidding the invasion from being referred to as anything besides a special military operation.
sentences.zh: 同一天，议会下院国家杜马通过了一项法律，禁止将这次入侵称为“特别军事行动”以外的任何名称。

sentences.en: Simply calling it a war or an invasion, instead of a special military operation, can lead to up to 15 years behind bars.
sentences.zh: 仅仅称其为战争或入侵，而不是特别军事行动，可能会导致最高15年的监禁。

sentences.en: And it essentially criminalizes independent reporting on the war.
sentences.zh: 这实际上将关于战争的独立报道定为犯罪。

sentences.en: Staff at one of Russia's most prominent independent television stations have resigned live on air.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯最著名的独立电视台之一的员工在直播中辞职。

sentences.en: And because of this law, the few remaining media outlets left in Russia are being forced to make really hard decisions.
sentences.zh: 由于这项法律，俄罗斯仅存的几家媒体被迫做出非常艰难的决定。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin and the authorities, they just don't want free media.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京和当局，他们就是不想要自由媒体。

sentences.en: This voice of truth must be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 这种真理的声音必须被摧毁。

sentences.en: Which means that right now there's only one version of events that Russians are seeing in their country.
sentences.zh: 这意味着现在俄罗斯人在国内只能看到一个版本的事件。

sentences.en: Putin's.
sentences.zh: 普京的版本。

sentences.en: This is a fundamentally different level of censorship.
sentences.zh: 这是一种根本不同层级的审查。

sentences.en: It's something we haven't seen since Soviet times.
sentences.zh: 这是我们自苏联时代以来从未见过的。

sentences.en: That's right, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 没错，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: And while it's not clear just how long Putin can sustain his attempts to seal off Russians' access to information about the war,
sentences.zh: 虽然目前还不清楚普京能维持多久他封锁俄罗斯人获取战争信息渠道的企图，

sentences.en: for now, he's been able to dramatically shape their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，他已经能够极大地塑造他们的信仰。

sentences.en: I'm not angry about my father.
sentences.zh: 我并不生我父亲的气。

sentences.en: I'm angry about Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 我生克里姆林宫的气。

sentences.en: I'm angry about the Russian propaganda.
sentences.zh: 我生俄罗斯宣传机器的气。

sentences.en: I'm not angry about these people.
sentences.zh: 我并不生这些人的气。

sentences.en: I understand that I cannot blame them in this situation.
sentences.zh: 我明白在这种情况下我不能责怪他们。

sentences.en: And that's forced people like Misha to try to convince his dad of the brutal truth of what's happening in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这迫使像米沙这样的人试图让他父亲相信乌克兰正在发生的残酷真相。

sentences.en: What do you think it is psychologically that prevents him from...
sentences.zh: 你认为在心理上是什么阻碍了他……

sentences.en: I mean, of course, there's this media, but you're also his son and you're telling him the truth and he doesn't want to believe it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然有这些媒体的影响，但你也是他的儿子，你在告诉他真相，而他却不想相信？

sentences.en: It's too painful?
sentences.zh: 太痛苦了吗？

sentences.en: It's too sad?
sentences.zh: 太悲伤了吗？

sentences.en: I think he won't.
sentences.zh: 我想他不会相信的。

sentences.en: I think he won't.
sentences.zh: 我想他不会相信的。

sentences.en: I think he won't.
sentences.zh: 我想他不会相信的。

sentences.en: He cannot.
sentences.zh: 他做不到。

sentences.en: He won't.
sentences.zh: 他不会的。

sentences.en: He loves me.
sentences.zh: 他爱我。

sentences.en: And he's really scared.
sentences.zh: 而且他真的很害怕。

sentences.en: And he told that his heart is bleeding.
sentences.zh: 他说他的心在滴血。

sentences.en: And that's very painful.
sentences.zh: 那非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And that's why we need to be more wise.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们需要更明智。

sentences.en: And we need to, like, be calm and explain and explain and explain.
sentences.zh: 我们需要保持冷静，不断地解释，解释，再解释。

sentences.en: Three times, so five times, so 20 times.
sentences.zh: 三次，五次，二十次。

sentences.en: As more as we need.
sentences.zh: 只要我们需要。

sentences.en: Valerie, thank you.
sentences.zh: 瓦莱丽，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: On Monday, the Associated Press reported that one of the pregnant women photographed in last week's attack by Russia on a maternity hospital in the city of Mariupol has died.
sentences.zh: 周一，美联社报道称，上周俄罗斯袭击马里乌波尔市一家妇产医院时被拍摄到的孕妇中，有一人已经死亡。

sentences.en: Her baby was delivered, but died too.
sentences.zh: 她的孩子被接生出来，但也死了。

sentences.en: The attack, and Russia's response to it, is an example of Russia presenting an alternate reality in the face of facts about the war.
sentences.zh: 这次袭击以及俄罗斯对此的回应，是俄罗斯在战争事实面前呈现另一种现实的一个例子。

sentences.en: After the bombing, Russia's defense ministry denied having done it, accusing Ukraine of a, quote, staged provocation.
sentences.zh: 轰炸后，俄罗斯国防部否认是其所为，指责乌克兰进行了所谓的“摆拍挑衅”。

sentences.en: Then Russia began to criticize the reaction with its foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, calling the international response to the bombing, quote, pathetic.
sentences.zh: 随后俄罗斯开始批评这一反应，其外交部长谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫称国际社会对轰炸的反应是“可悲的”。

sentences.en: And that global public opinion had been, quote, manipulated.
sentences.zh: 并称全球舆论受到了“操纵”。

sentences.en: It's not the first time we see pathetic outcries concerning the so-called atrocities.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们第一次看到关于所谓暴行的可悲呼声。

sentences.en: You could draw your own conclusions as to how the public opinion is manipulated worldwide.
sentences.zh: 你可以自己得出关于全球舆论是如何被操纵的结论。

sentences.en: Finally,
sentences.zh: 最后，

sentences.en: Russia's embassy in London tweeted photographs of one of the women and claimed that she was a crisis actor who had played several of the women photographed in the immediate aftermath of the attack.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯驻伦敦大使馆在推特上发布了其中一名妇女的照片，并声称她是一名危机演员，在袭击发生后的第一时间扮演了多名被拍摄的妇女。

sentences.en: Twitter eventually removed the poSt.
sentences.zh: 推特最终删除了这条帖子。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Russia attacked a Ukrainian military base 12 miles from Ukraine's border with Poland, bringing the war dangerously close to NATO's doorstep.
sentences.zh: 周日，俄罗斯袭击了距离乌克兰与波兰边境12英里的一个乌克兰军事基地，使战争危险地接近北约的家门口。

sentences.en: The target was a base used to train foreign fighters who flocked to Ukraine to help defend the country against Russia.
sentences.zh: 目标是一个用于训练外国战斗人员的基地，他们涌入乌克兰以帮助保卫国家抵御俄罗斯。

sentences.en: The missile attack killed at least 35 people and wounded at least 134.
sentences.zh: 导弹袭击造成至少35人死亡，至少134人受伤。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the death count has risen sharply in the city of Mediopol, which has been encircled and bombed by Russian troops and has been without power, water,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，马里乌波尔市的死亡人数急剧上升，该市已被俄罗斯军队包围并轰炸，且已经断电、断水、

sentences.en: or phone connection for more than 10 days.
sentences.zh: 或断开电话联系超过10天。

sentences.en: So far, city officials said, the Russian attacks have killed 2,187 residents.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，市政府官员表示，俄罗斯的袭击已造成2187名居民死亡。

sentences.en: Finally, Russian forces have kidnapped a second Ukrainian mayor in what appears to be a strategy of removing local officials and replacing them with Russian puppets.
sentences.zh: 最后，俄罗斯军队绑架了第二位乌克兰市长，这似乎是一种撤换地方官员并以俄罗斯傀儡取而代之的策略。

sentences.en: The abduction of the mayor from the town of Dniproprudne follows the dramatic capture of the mayor of Melitopol,
sentences.zh: 继梅利托波尔市长被戏剧性地抓捕后，第聂伯鲁德内镇的市长也被绑架，

sentences.en: who was reportedly taken from a government building with a bag over his head.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他被蒙着头从政府大楼带走。

sentences.en: In a video message, the mayor's replacement, a Russian appointee, instructed the residents of Melitopol to adjust to, quote,
sentences.zh: 在一段视频信息中，市长的继任者，一名俄罗斯任命的官员，指示梅利托波尔的居民适应所谓的“

sentences.en: the new reality and to end their resistance to Russian occupation.
sentences.zh: 新现实”，并结束他们对俄罗斯占领的抵抗。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asla Chaturvedi, Diana Nguyen, and Caitlin Roberts, with help from Rob Zipko and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯拉·查图尔维迪、戴安娜·阮和凯特琳·罗伯茨制作，罗布·齐普科和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George and Lisa Chow, contains original music by Marian Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格一起，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。
